chg1.text: Round five starts the clock on the day the money arrives, and runs for two years. Each campaign has all of its money on day zero. The facility is ready between day 60 and day 100, and the equipment is ordered on day zero: some of it used, chosen by a rule.

chg1.phonemes: ɹˈaʊnd fˈaɪv stˈɑːɹts ðə klˈɑːk ɔnðə dˈeɪ ðə mˈʌni ɚɹˈaɪvz, ænd ɹˈʌnz fɔːɹ tˈuː jˈɪɹz. ˈiːtʃ kæmpˈeɪn hɐz ˈɔːl ʌv ɪts mˈʌni ˌɔn dˈeɪ zˈiəɹoʊ. ðə fəsˈɪlᵻɾi ɪz ɹˈɛdi bᵻtwˌiːn dˈeɪ sˈɪksti ænd dˈeɪ wˈʌnhˈʌndɹɪd, ænd ðɪ ɪkwˈɪpmənt ɪz ˈɔːɹdɚd ˌɔn dˈeɪ zˈiəɹoʊ: sˌʌm ʌv ɪt jˈuːzd, tʃˈoʊzən baɪ ɐ ɹˈuːl.

chg2.text: Experiments also start on day zero, through partners, while the lab is built. Decisions made by people take time. The conventional lab's atomizer runs at most 8 times a week; the automated lab's runs around the clock once its cell is integrated. And the HPC computes candidates continuously. Every lead time, price and decision window here is a stand-in.

cnt1.text: Three counters run through the replay. Designed means computed candidates: a stream on the HPC evaluates 122,880 a day, at full capacity and outside the experiments' cost. The policy sees 64 new ones a day.

cnt2.text: Made means powder lots, or alloys made. Tested means alloys through the full chain: in the replayed run, 104 aluminium alloys and 6 copper alloys.

cnt4.text: In the replay's plots, the solid curve is the best new alloy tested so far in the automated lab, and the dashed curve is the conventional lab, on the same seed and policy. The dotted lines are the two targets.

cnt5.text: Money is shown as cumulative spend in each lab, not as a budget bar. And when best so far goes flat, the replay says why.
cnt5.spoken: Money is shown as cumulative spend in each lab, not as a budget bar. And when best so far goes flat, the replay says why.

atm1.text: Once its cell is integrated, the automated lab's atomizer runs around the clock at a derived cycle: about 2.2 hours per aluminium composition, or 76 a week. That is a design target, not a demonstrated rate.

atm2.text: It needs 6 to 8 pre-coated crucibles per alloy family in rotation, and the lab has one. The lab's record so far is 10 runs in 43 days, about 1.6 a week. Before the cell, and in the conventional lab, the twin assumes 8 a week.

note1.text: Everything here is simulated: the alloys, the results, and every measurement, with modelled noise not yet calibrated on the lab's instruments. The facility window, every lead time, the used-equipment prices, the decision windows, the HPC allocation, and the atomizer's design cycle are assumptions and stand-ins. It shows how two lab designs and their policies interact in a model, not what the real lab will find.
